questions.explanation:
A complete binary tree is a binary tree where all levels, except possibly the last, are filled, and all 
nodes are as left as possible. Consider the tree shown below. This has 8 nodes more than the 
original tree (nodes 5, 6, 7, 11, 22, 26, 28, and 30), which is the minimum number of nodes 
required. This is because the original binary tree consisted of 5 levels (level 0 [root] through level 
4 [leaves]), so levels 0 through 3 must be complexly filled (i.e., perfect), and all missing children 
left of node 17 (i.e., the right-most leaf in the original tree) must be filled. There are 5 missing 
internal nodes on levels 0 through 3, and 3 missing leaf nodes on level 4.
